nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $n$ and $b \ge 2$ be natural numbers. If the base-$b$ representation of $p^n$ is a palindrome with an even number of digits, then $b = p^x - 1$ for some natural number $x$.
nodes.title: Even-length palindromic prime powers have base one less than a power of the prime

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b \ge 2$ be natural numbers. If the base-$b$ representation of $2^n$ is a palindrome with an even number of digits, then $b = 2^x - 1$ for some natural number $x$.
nodes.title: Even-length palindromic powers of 2 have base one less than a power of 2

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $b \ge 2$, $\alpha \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be natural numbers. If the base-$b$ digits of $2^n$, from the most significant to the least significant, are $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$, then $b = 2^x - 1$ for some natural number $x \le n$, and $\alpha = 2^i$ for some natural number $i$.
nodes.title: Bases of binomial forms of powers of 2

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \ge 1$, $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $\alpha\binom{k}{\lceil k/2 \rceil} < b$. Then the base-$b$ representation of $\alpha(1 + b)^k$ has exactly the $k + 1$ digits $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$, from the most significant to the least significant.
nodes.title: Digits of a multiple of a power of one more than the base

nodes.summary: Let $z \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural numbers. Then the base-$z$ digits of $z^n$ are a $1$ followed by $n$ zeros, and, if $n \ge 1$, the base-$z$ digits of $z^n + 1$ are a $1$, then $n - 1$ zeros, then a $1$.
nodes.title: Digits of a power of the base and of its successor

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 2$ there are natural numbers $y$ and $b$ with $y \le \lceil \sqrt{2n} \rceil + 1$ and $2 \le b \le 2^y - 1$ such that $2^n$ has a base-$b$ representation in binomial form.
nodes.title: Powers of 2 have binomial forms in small bases

nodes.summary: The number $2023$ has a base-$16$ representation in binomial form: its base-$16$ digits are $7, 14, 7$, that is $7\binom{2}{2}, 7\binom{2}{1}, 7\binom{2}{0}$.
nodes.title: The binomial form of 2023 in base 16

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $x$, $k$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 1$, $n = xk + r$ and $2^r\binom{k}{\lceil k/2 \rceil} < 2^x - 1$. Then $2^n$ has a base-$(2^x - 1)$ representation in binomial form.
nodes.title: Sufficient condition for a binomial form of a power of 2

nodes.summary: A natural number $N$ has a base-$b$ representation in binomial form if there are natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ such that the base-$b$ digits of $N$, from the most significant to the least significant, are $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$.
nodes.title: Binomial form

nodes.summary: Let $N \ge 1$ be a natural number and let $b(N)$ be the smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which $N$ is a palindrome. If $b(N) = N - 1$, then $N \in \{3, 4, 6\}$, or $N > 6$ and $N$ is prime.
nodes.title: Brown's theorem on minimal palindromic base one less than the number

nodes.summary: The smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which the number $2$ is a palindrome is $b(2) = 3$: in base $2$ the number $2$ is written $(1, 0)_2$, which is not a palindrome, while in base $3$ it is the one-digit palindrome $(2)_3$.
nodes.title: The minimum palindromic base of two

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, $b(N)$ is the smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which $N$ is a palindrome, that is, in which the base-$b$ digits of $N$ read the same forwards and backwards. Such a base exists: $0$ has no digits and is a palindrome in every base, and for $N \ge 1$ the number $N$ is written with the single digit $N$ in base $N + 1$.
nodes.title: Minimum palindromic base

nodes.summary: Let $x, y, n, q$ be natural numbers with $x \ge 2$, $y \ge 2$, $n \ge 3$ and $q \ge 2$ such that $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^q$. If $q = 2$, or $3 \mid n$, or $4 \mid n$, or $q = 3$ and $n \not\equiv 5 \pmod 6$, then $(x, y, n, q)$ is one of $(3, 11, 5, 2)$, $(7, 20, 4, 2)$ and $(18, 7, 3, 3)$; these are $11^2 = (1,1,1,1,1)_3$, $20^2 = (1,1,1,1)_7$ and $7^3 = (1,1,1)_{18}$.
nodes.title: The Nagell–Ljunggren equation in natural numbers (Bugeaud–Mihăilescu)

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $b \ge 2$ a base. There is a digit $c \ne 2$ such that the base-$b$ representation of $2^n$ is $(1, c, 1)_b$, that is, $2^n = 1 + cb + b^2$ with $0 \le c < b$, if and only if (i) $2^n - 1 = kb$ for some natural number $k$ with $b \le k \le 2b - 1$, and (ii) it is not the case that $n$ is even and $b = 2^{n/2} - 1$.
nodes.title: Three-digit representations of powers of two with outer digits one

nodes.summary: Let $x \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $b = 2^x - 1$, and suppose that the base-$b$ representation $2^n = (c_k, \dots, c_0)_b$ is a palindrome with $k + 1$ digits. Then (1) $n > k(x - 1)$; and (2) if $n = kx + r$ for a natural number $r$, and either $k \le x - r$, or $3 \le k \le x - r + 1$ and $x \ge 3$, then $c_i = 2^r \binom{k}{i}$ for $i = 0, \dots, k$, that is, the representation is the binomial…
nodes.title: Palindromic powers of two in a base one less than a power of two

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and let $N$ be a natural number whose base-$b$ digits form a palindrome with an even number of digits. Then $b + 1$ divides $N$.
nodes.title: Even-length palindromes are divisible by the base plus one

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $\alpha \ge 1$ be natural numbers and let $b \ge 2$ be a base. The base-$b$ representation of $2^n$ is $(\alpha, 2\alpha, \alpha)_b$ if and only if there is a natural number $i$ with $3i + 2 < n$, $n \equiv i \pmod 2$, $\alpha = 2^i$ and $b = 2^{(n - i)/2} - 1$.
nodes.title: Three-digit binomial forms of powers of two

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $b \ge 2$ be a base, and let $c = 2^n \bmod b$. The base-$b$ representation of $2^n$ is a palindrome with exactly three digits if and only if $b^2 + 1 \le 2^n \le b^3 - 1$, $c \ne 0$, and $\frac{1}{b} \lfloor 2^n / b \rfloor - \frac{b - 1}{b} \le c \le \frac{1}{b} \lfloor 2^n / b \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Three-digit palindromic powers of two
